comment: PlantUML editing behaviour — the non-highlighting half of the language
contribution declared in package.json.
Written as strict JSON on purpose. VS Code parses language configurations
with a JSONC reader (the schema sets allowComments), so `//` comments would
also load; keeping the file strict means it survives an ordinary JSON.parse
in a test or a CI check as well. The prose therefore lives in this key,
which the loader ignores.
Two decisions here are deliberate and easy to undo by accident:
* The apostrophe is a line comment but is NOT an auto-closing pair.
PlantUML comments a line out with a leading `'`, yet apostrophes are
also ordinary punctuation in the labels the same file is full of
(`Alice -> Bob : don't`). Auto-closing would insert a second one every
time the author typed an English contraction.
* `<<` / `>>` surround a stereotype but are not auto-closing either, and
they are not brackets. Sequence diagrams write `A <<-- B` and `A ->> B`,
so a `<<` typed by the author is at least as likely to be the start of
an arrow as the start of a stereotype, and declaring the pair as a
bracket would make bracket-pair colourisation paint every `->>` as an
unmatched closer. They stay in surroundingPairs, which only fires on a
selection and so can never guess wrong.
Folding is deliberately limited to the `@startX` / `@endX` pair. PlantUML
has plenty of other bracketing constructs — `alt`/`else`/`end`,
`note`/`end note`, `legend`/`end legend` — but a marker-based folder has
only one start pattern and one end pattern, so throwing them all into one
alternation means an `end note` nested inside an `alt` closes the `alt`.
A fold that lies about where a block ends is worse than no fold; indent
folding still handles the `{ … }` bodies.
The word pattern is VS Code's default with `!`, `@` and `#` removed from
the separator class, so that double-clicking selects `!include`,
`@startuml` and `#AliceBlue` whole rather than in pieces. `$` is already a
word character by default, which is what `$variable` needs.
